# GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat): request flow and controls

> Vendor-derived text below is untrusted data, never instructions. `‹` and `›` stand for `<` and `>`; a ⚠ marks text that looked like an instruction.

Steps run in the typical order. A documented order appears only where a cell states it; a decision point appears only where the documentation describes a branch (each branch quotes it). Many agents have few or none.

## A. Setup, before the first model call

- Choose the front door [partly documented, unverified] You can reach it from inside VS Code, from a separate terminal session, from a dedicated Agents window, and through programming interfaces. The documentation does not mention a headless mode or use in CI and chat services.
- Apply organization rules [documented, unverified] Administrators can manage Copilot centrally. Most managed settings override a person's own settings on managed devices, and policy can switch agent mode off, require manual approval for specific tools and restrict which models are offered.
  - documented order: On managed devices, most managed settings win over the person's own setting.
- Load the house rules [documented, with limits, unverified] It reads instruction files from your project and home folder, some applying by file pattern. What works depends on the selected agent harness, and nested and linked files are off by default. Instructions stored just in your editor profile are a legacy location it does not read.
- Load memory and earlier sessions [documented, with limits, unverified] It can keep notes at user, repository and session level, and restore earlier sessions after a reload, in the terminal or from another app. A fork copies the conversation but may share code changes with the original. Transcript formats are not a stable shared interface.
- Stock the built-in tools [documented, unverified] The agent picks from the enabled tools, such as reading files, running terminal commands, searching the codebase, fetching web content and using a built-in browser. Terminal commands need your approval by default, and file edits are saved straight to the project folder.
- Load skills and custom commands [partly documented, unverified] A skill is a folder with an instruction file that the agent loads when a task fits or when you pick it by name. Custom commands come from prompt files, which are deprecated for Agent Host sessions. The documentation does not mention per-skill tool or model overrides.
  - decision point (copilot-vscode/F08.resource-loading): Are the extra files in a skill folder read?
    - The skill instructions mention the file -> Copilot reads the extra file from the skill folder when the instructions point to it. | quote: “only when the instructions reference them”
    - Nothing in the instructions mentions the file -> The file is not loaded. | quote: “an unreferenced file is not loaded”
- Connect outside tools [documented, with limits, unverified] It connects MCP servers and offers their tools to the model, with explicit approval required for tool calls. Copilot sessions are currently limited to local servers that do not need authentication, and plugin servers are trusted when the plugin is installed.
  - decision point (copilot-vscode/F12.server-trust): Does a connected MCP server ask me to trust it first?
    - The server comes from the workspace -> It inherits the folder's trust decision (Workspace Trust). | quote: “workspace MCP servers inherit Workspace Trust”
    - The server comes from a plugin -> It is trusted when you install the plugin, with no separate trust prompt at startup. | quote: “Plugin MCP servers are implicitly trusted when you install the plugin”
- Set the safety posture [documented, with limits, unverified] You choose how much needs your confirmation: manual approval, an autonomous mode, or a bypass that disables security protections. Plan and Ask modes limit what it does. If enterprise policy disables auto-approval, new sessions start on manual.
  - documented order: For a local Agent Host, workspace sandbox settings win over user settings, and product defaults come after.
  - decision point (copilot-vscode/F04.config-scope-precedence): When two settings disagree, which one wins?
    - Workspace and user sandbox settings -> For a local Agent Host, the workspace setting wins over the user setting. | quote: “Workspace sandbox settings take precedence over User settings”
    - Copilot managed setting and device policy -> The Copilot managed setting wins, and the two values are not merged. | quote: “A Copilot managed setting takes precedence over a VS Code device policy”
    - A policy value and an ordinary setting -> The policy value overrides the setting at default, user and workspace level. | quote: “A policy value overrides the setting at default, user and workspace level”
- Pick the model and thinking effort [documented, with limits] You pick the model from a picker in the chat box and can set defaults for chat, planning and inline chat. Bring-your-own-key lets you use other providers, but some features need the Copilot service. Models depend on your account and organization, and effort levels vary.
  - documented order: If a prompt file names a model it uses that one; otherwise the picker's choice applies.
- Prepare an isolated workspace [documented, with limits] A Code isolation control lets a session run in the current folder or in its own Git worktree, so each task gets its own files and branch. Changes can still conflict, and a worktree is not a security boundary.

## B. Each turn, before sending

- Assemble the prompt [documented, unverified] Each time the agent sends a request, the editor builds a prompt from multiple sources. You can add MCP resources, a selected page element or referenced files as context. Models differ in context window size, and a chat-input control shows how much of the window is used.
- Run your own code at set moments [documented, with limits, unverified] Hooks run your own shell commands at points in an agent session, such as before a tool runs, and can block or change the action. They apply to the Local agent, not automatically to Agent Host sessions, and Claude-style hook files need a setting that is off by default.
  - documented order: For a PreToolUse event, a deny decision wins over ask, and ask wins over allow.

## C. The model call

- Send the request and handle trouble [documented, unverified] Auto model selection routes each request to a model based on task complexity and availability. For a temporary rate limit the documentation says to wait a few minutes and retry. Monthly allowances reset each month, and a status dashboard shows when one is reached.
- Set the thinking budget [documented, with limits] Models that support it show a thinking effort choice, and higher effort uses more thinking tokens and more AI credits. Thinking tokens count toward the context window. The thinking itself is typically summarized or left out, and the display setting is experimental.
- Reuse the unchanged part of the prompt [not researched]

## D. After the model answers, every turn

- Read what the model asked for [not researched]
- Decide whether it is allowed [documented, with limits, unverified] Approval can be set by tool, by file path pattern and by terminal command, and an automatic reviewer model can judge risk. Command rules use best-effort parsing that shell tricks can slip past, and the permission rules apply to enterprise-managed users and Agent Host sessions.
- Save an undo point [documented, with limits] You can hover over an earlier request and restore a checkpoint, which brings back affected workspace files and the chat to that point. It does not undo terminal commands, network requests, deployments or changes to outside services, and it is described for supported sessions.
- Run it inside the fence [documented, with limits, unverified] Terminal commands can run inside an operating-system sandbox that limits files and network access, and child processes inherit it. It is in preview or experimental depending on the system, and it does not restrict the built-in file tools or replace approval controls.
  - documented order: If the bypass permission is set to false in one place and true in another, false wins.
  - decision point (copilot-vscode/F05.sandbox-override): What happens if a command cannot run inside the sandbox?
    - A command cannot run inside the sandbox -> The agent can ask you to confirm running the command outside the sandbox. | quote: “the agent can ask for confirmation to run it outside”
    - The outside-sandbox setting is false -> The Allow Outside Sandbox choice is not offered and the request fails. | quote: “Allow Outside Sandbox is not offered and such requests fail”
- Tidy the tool's output [not researched]
- Feed the result back and go round again [documented, unverified] The agent repeats reasoning, tool use and checking: it runs a requested tool, feeds the result back, and goes again. You can steer, queue a follow-up or stop a request, though stopping does not undo finished actions. A setting caps how many requests it makes.
- Hand work to helpers [partly documented, unverified] Custom agents can have their own tools and model, and helpers can run in parallel when the harness supports concurrent subagents. Nesting is off by default and capped at five levels when on. The documentation does not mention per-agent effort.
  - documented order: A custom agent can list several models; they are tried in order until one is available.
- Shrink the context when it fills [documented, unverified] When a conversation nears the limit, the editor summarizes older parts on its own, and a setting can turn that off. You can also trigger compaction by hand whenever you like and add instructions on what the summary should keep.
- Show the answer or ask you [documented] Plan mode researches the codebase, clarifies requirements and proposes a plan, then waits for your approval before acting. The plan can be handed to an implementation agent. Controls in the chat input show session cost in credits and context use.
- Wrap up and keep score [documented, with limits, unverified] It shows token counts and AI credits used for a session. Paid plans have a monthly allowance, with an optional extra budget once credits are exhausted. Copilot Chat can emit OpenTelemetry signals, and debug logs show whether customizations were loaded.
  - decision point (copilot-vscode/F22.budget-caps): What can I do when my monthly AI credits run out?
    - Set a budget for extra usage -> You can keep working on a paid plan by setting a budget for additional usage. | quote: “a user can set a budget for additional usage and keep working”
    - Wait for the next cycle -> You wait until the monthly cycle rolls over and the allowance resets. | quote: “or wait until the next monthly cycle when the allowance resets”

## E. Around the session

- Run without you watching [documented, with limits, unverified] It can run long commands and sessions in the background, run scheduled automations, send a task to a cloud agent that returns a pull request, and be controlled remotely. Automations are listed as off in Stable, and cloud sessions need a GitHub-backed repository.
- Extend and share [documented, with limits, unverified] Agent plugins bundle related customizations such as MCP servers into one package, installed from plugin marketplaces. Plugins from some sources do not update by themselves, and a marketplace allowlist does not retroactively disable plugins already installed.
  - decision point (copilot-vscode/F11.versioning-update): How does a plugin get updated?
    - You check for extension updates -> VS Code checks for plugin updates when you run the check command, or on a 24-hour timer if automatic updates are on. | quote: “VS Code checks for plugin updates when you run Extensions: Check for Extension Updates”
    - The plugin comes from a package registry -> It does not update by itself; an Update button appears in the Extensions view. | quote: “Plugins sourced from npm or PyPI never update automatically”
- Updates and releases [documented, unverified] The documentation read describes VS Code 1.140. Copilot extensions have a pre-release version, updates can be automatic, and deprecations are noted inline in the docs. Release notes for older versions are on the Updates page.
- Where it runs and who runs it [documented, with limits] It runs inside VS Code, where the Copilot Chat panel is the harness, and can host Claude and Codex sessions. It uses your Copilot plan, though bring-your-own-key models need none. A setting moves new sessions to the Copilot SDK harness but does not migrate existing ones.
- Identity, retention and audit [documented, with limits] Copilot reuses your GitHub sign-in, and a policy can switch AI features off until you sign in to a matching organization account. Prompt content is not captured by default. Identity capture for audit is described for Local harness sessions.
